option.label: Long hairs along blade margins
option.detail: Trace hairs to the blade edge. Gould permits smooth blades or long stiff hairs along margins and sometimes the upper surface near the ligule. Raised papilla bases are not established.

option.label: Flowering branch axis flattened and winged
option.detail: Inspect the flowering branch under its two rows of overlapping spikelets. This winged rachis is not a keel on the sheath or a groove on a spikelet pedicel.

option.label: UPPER glume has 5–7 veins
option.detail: Count veins on the SECOND (upper) outer glume. Gould separately states that the FIRST glume has one vein. Do not transfer either count to a lemma.

option.label: Lemma has three veins
option.detail: Open the outer glumes before counting veins on an INNER lemma. Gould describes three-veined lemmas; upper glume veins are a separate character.

option.label: Lemma laterally compressed and keeled
option.detail: Inspect one floret in side and face views. Gould describes a somewhat laterally compressed lemma with an acute or obtuse, sometimes minutely pointed tip. A keel or tiny point is not a true awn.

exact_awn_absence.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O’Kennon (1999), Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas, exact Eleusine indica, printed p.1268
exact_awn_absence.note: Exact species account explicitly describes awnless spikelets. Gould pp.222–223 permits only a slight lemma mucro. A verified true lemma awn contradicts this account; a pointed or mucronate tip, an awnless partner, or uncertain novice bristle does not.
exact_awn_absence.stage_caution: Confirm the structure is an attached true lemma awn on the observed grass, not a tiny mucro or a neighboring plant.

learner_diagnostic_checks.look: Separate a true lemma awn from a minute pointed tip
learner_diagnostic_checks.check: Diggs explicitly describes awnless spikelets; Gould permits a slight lemma mucro. A verified true lemma awn, including the KR 1–1.5 mm fertile-awn choice, conflicts with goosegrass. A tiny point or the broad beginner short-bristle choice alone is insufficient.
learner_diagnostic_checks.compare: KR awn length differs between sources; use the organ actually observed, not an assumed species identity.
learner_diagnostic_checks.certainty: Exact Diggs p.1268 absence statement, with Gould tip qualification; no local specimen certified.
learner_diagnostic_checks.source: Frank W. Gould (1975), The Grasses of Texas, exact Eleusine indica, printed pp.222–223

learner_diagnostic_checks.look: Count florets, then identify the two outer glumes
learner_diagnostic_checks.check: Gould describes 3–6 florets inside each spikelet. The first glume has one vein; the larger second has 5–7. Inner lemmas have three veins. Do not confuse several florets with several spikelets or transfer a vein count between organs.
learner_diagnostic_checks.compare: KR sessile/stalked spikelet pairs are not several florets inside one goosegrass spikelet.
learner_diagnostic_checks.certainty: Gould p.223; preserve supplementary numerical variation.
learner_diagnostic_checks.source: Frank W. Gould (1975), The Grasses of Texas, exact Eleusine indica, printed pp.222–223

learner_diagnostic_checks.look: Inspect flattened winged flowering branches and compressed sheaths
learner_diagnostic_checks.check: Goosegrass is a tufted leafy annual, occasionally stoloniferous at base. Usually 2–11 fingers carry sessile overlapping spikelets in two rows on flattened winged axes; one or two branches can arise below the summit. Sheaths are compressed and strongly keeled; ligule is a ciliate membrane about 1 mm.
learner_diagnostic_checks.compare: Tuft, basal runners and fingerlike heads can overlap KR. A flowering rachis wing differs from a KR pedicel groove.
learner_diagnostic_checks.certainty: Exact Gould pp.222–223, corroborated by Diggs p.1268; branch count is variable.
learner_diagnostic_checks.source: Frank W. Gould (1975), The Grasses of Texas, exact Eleusine indica, printed pp.222–223

secondary_reference_review.corroborates: Annual; decumbent/erect culms 15–65 cm; compressed keeled pilose-margined sheaths; short membrane; digitate/subdigitate branches; awnless overlapping spikelets in two rows on flat winged axes.

non_scoring_context.fruit: Loose caryopsis, transversely ridged and rugose; seed loosely enclosed by thin pericarp.
non_scoring_context.historical_flowering: Mostly late summer/autumn; occasionally late spring.
